title: A Landfall for the Compass
premise: Wren Nakamura flies supply runs into a rainforest river country where the law is a rumor and her past is a debt she's been outrunning for six years. When the Halvorsen expedition upriver goes silent, the company that owns their contract pressures Wren to retrieve them quietly—and to bring back whatever they found sealed in the old survey vault. She discovers the expedition uncovered evidence that could topple the company's land claims, and that one member, a cartographer named Ilsa, chose to stay behind to protect it. To bring everyone home alive, Wren must choose between erasing what was found—buying her own freedom—and letting the truth surface, knowing it will cost her the anonymity she's built her life on. In the end she flies the evidence out herself, testifies under her real name, and finds that the found family of the river camp is worth more than invisibility ever was.
about_author: Zephyrine Vasquez is a former bush-strip radio operator who spent four years in remote river settlements before turning to fiction. Her work explores how people build families in places the law forgot.

chapters.title: Fuel, Weather, Debt
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A routine medicine run establishes her world: the airstrip at Puerto Cielo, her battered De Havilland, and the ledger of favors she owes the company man, Reyes. Emotional beat: weary competence masking a woman who has made smallness a survival strategy.

chapters.title: The Silence on 126.7
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Halvorsen expedition misses three scheduled check-ins. Reyes offers to forgive part of Wren's debt if she flies upriver to investigate—alone, off the books. Beat: temptation wrapped in a trap; she accepts because debt always wins.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, flying north through storm cells. Flashbacks to the incident six years ago that created her debt and drove her from her name. Beat: dread layered over muscle memory as the landscape turns hostile.

chapters.title: Camp Empty, Kettle Warm
chapters.summary: Wren lands at the abandoned expedition camp: gear intact, radio smashed, a map half-burned in the fire pit. She finds fresh tracks leading toward the old survey vault. Beat: cold fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Wouldn't Leave
chapters.summary: Introduces Tam, the expedition's sixteen-year-old radio tech, hiding in a cave, half-starved. His POV reveals the team split after finding something in the vault. Beat: Wren's armor cracks—she can't leave him, and he won't let her turn back.

chapters.title: Compass Points
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Tam carries his father's compass—the same model as hers, a coincidence that unsettles her. They follow the burned map toward the vault, pursued by signs someone else is tracking them. Beat: wary alliance forming into trust.

chapters.title: Reyes on the Wire
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Reyes in Puerto Cielo, who reports to the company that Wren is en route and must not come back with documents. Beat: dramatic irony—the reader sees the net closing while Wren flies blind.

chapters.title: The Vault Door
chapters.summary: Wren and Tam reach the vault and find it breached from inside. They're ambushed by Mercer, the expedition's security chief, who holds them at gunpoint but hesitates—he's not sure whose side pays better anymore. Beat: terror, then uneasy truce.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Ledger
chapters.summary: Inside the vault: survey records proving the company falsified boundary lines to seize indigenous land. Cartographer Ilsa Voss left a coded note directing them to her hiding place downstream. Beat: revelation reframes everything—this isn't rescue, it's testimony.

chapters.title: Mercer's Price
chapters.summary: Mercer's POV. His backstory as a man who sold his conscience by installments. He agrees to guide them to Ilsa—for a cut of whatever leverage the documents buy. Beat: moral ambiguity deepens; even the hired gun wants out.

chapters.title: Rapids and Reckoning
chapters.summary: The three travel downriver by stolen boat through rapids. Tam nearly drowns; Wren pulls him out and finally tells him a piece of her past. Beat: found family crystallizing under pressure.

chapters.title: The Company Man Arrives
chapters.summary: Reyes flies in with hired men, landing at the downstream mission where Ilsa hides. Wren learns of it via the mission's shortwave. Beat: clock starts ticking hard—hours, not days.

chapters.title: Ilsa Voss, Alive and Stubborn
chapters.summary: They reach Ilsa, wounded but defiant, guarding copies of the records. She refuses to run: 'Documents don't testify. People do.' Beat: clash of philosophies—invisibility versus standing in the light.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Mission
chapters.summary: Mercer sells their location to Reyes, then regrets it when the company men open fire instead of negotiating. Gunfight in the mission courtyard; Mercer takes a bullet shielding Tam. Beat: betrayal and redemption colliding in one breath.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Reyes's men disable Wren's plane. Trapped, the group plans a desperate move: repair the plane using mission parts while Ilsa broadcasts the evidence to every settlement on the band. Beat: despair transmuted into audacity.

chapters.title: Night Work
chapters.summary: Quiet chapter, Wren's POV. While soldering the fuel line, she and Ilsa talk about names—the ones we abandon, the ones we reclaim. Wren decides to use her real name when this ends. Beat: stillness before the storm; identity chosen, not fled.

chapters.title: Takeoff Under Fire
chapters.summary: Dawn takeoff through gunfire from the strip's edge. Mercer stays behind to hold the road, buying them minutes. Beat: white-knuckle action; sacrifice made without ceremony.

chapters.title: The Long Way Home
chapters.summary: Wren flies storm-wounded toward Puerto Cielo with Ilsa and Tam aboard, dodging a company charter sent to force her down. Aerial cat-and-mouse through cloud canyons. Beat: peak tension, skill as salvation.

chapters.title: Landing on a Borrowed Strip
chapters.summary: Forced to land short of town on a missionary grass strip, they're met—not by company men, but by river settlers Ilsa's broadcast reached, armed with radios and solidarity. Beat: the theme lands—justice outside the law arrives as community.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: In Puerto Cielo, before a regional magistrate and a room full of settlers, Wren gives her name aloud for the first time in six years and tells everything—including her own crime. Beat: catharsis; the debt paid not with money but with truth.

chapters.title: What the Court Couldn't Weigh
chapters.summary: Aftermath: the company's claims suspended, Reyes arrested, Mercer recovering in the mission infirmary. Wren is fined and briefly detained for her past—but walks free because the river vouched for her. Beat: justice imperfect but real.

chapters.title: A Landfall for the Compass
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Wren's POV. Months later she flies again—medicine, mail, and now passengers: Tam apprenticing as her radio op, Ilsa mapping honestly. The compass on her dash points home, not away. Beat: resolution; the woman who flew to disappear now flies to belong.
